title: Sharp reverse hypercontractivity
statement: Let $p,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<q$, $q<p$, $p<1$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\rho^2=(1-p)/(1-q)$. For every nonnegative real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube, $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$.
hypotheses_covered: p, q, and ρ are real
f is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
f is nonnegative at every cube point
replaced: Let $0<q<p<1$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\rho^2=(1-p)/(1-q)$. Every $f:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_p(f)$, where $M_r(u)=(\E|u|^r)^{1/r}$ under the uniform measure. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
